summary.intent: Consolidate one-off evaluation scripts into a single tested tool that measures agent cost, skill usage, gate rounds and tool-output share from session transcripts, and record the evaluation results in docs.
summary.outcome: Committed tools/transcript-metrics.py with tests/test_transcript_metrics.py, and a second commit adding docs/evaluations; task statuses were updated. The tool reproduced earlier totals on two real projects.

repo: Transcript analysis tooling lives in tools/transcript-metrics.py with tests in tests/test_transcript_metrics.py; evaluation write-ups go in docs/evaluations.
Commit messages follow conventional-commit style (feat(tooling), docs(evaluations)) and include a Claude-Session trailer URL.

The tool computes subagent tokens and minutes per agent type (with plugin share and a cost-cliff flag), skill vs agent invocations per session, rounds/blockers/retry counts/escalations per spec from persisted verdicts, and the share of tool output a compressor could reach.
workflow: Code and docs were committed separately (tool plus tests first, then evaluation docs) in a single chained git command.
Turning one-off analysis scripts into a tested tool let the results be validated by reproducing earlier totals on real projects.

open_items: Evaluation findings need follow-up: gates return blockers after a clean round, and passes are recorded above the retry cap.
The share of tool output a compressor could reach is measured, but no compressor is implemented in this session.
